niche.habitat: 2–10 m below ice shell (polar & equatorial zones)
niche.active: Continuous, peaks during tidal flexure & ice-quakes

body: Flat disc with ciliary fringes, ventral rasping mouth, dorsal crystalline plates

chains.trait: Ventral rasping mouth and flattened disc shape
links: Needs to cling to vertical ice without sinking in dense water
Low gravity (1.31 m/s²) plus high water density

skill.effect: It scrapes away thick biofilm mats and glides effortlessly across icy terrain.

chains.weakness: Dislodged by sudden pressure waves that break adhesion.

journal.en: It wears its food like a coat.

plausibility.summary: A flattened, adhering grazer with a ventral radula or rasp matches ice–ocean-interface epiphyte grazing under low g (F5) and high-density brine (F13–F15). Primary production is chemolithoautotrophic (F12, F20); dense microbial mats at redox/oxidant interfaces (F25) can support small macrograzers if turnover is slow (F24)—Riftia-scale giants are ruled out, limpet-scale grazers are not.
fixes: A flattened, adhering grazer with a ventral radula or rasp matches ice–ocean-interface epiphyte grazing under low g (F5) and high-density brine (F13–F15). Primary production is chemolithoautotrophic (F12, F20); dense microbial mats at redox/oxidant interfaces (F25) can support small macrograzers if turnover is slow (F24)—Riftia-scale giants are ruled out, limpet-scale grazers are not.

analogues.organism: Patellid limpets and chitons (radula scraping + firm attachment); subglacial and ice-shelf microbial mats at the water–ice contact (terrestrial analogue communities, not macrofauna at Europan scale).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Shields internal tissues from abrasive ice contact

skill.effect: Its crystalline plates absorb heavy blows, allowing it to recover strongly after taking a hit.

journal.en: It carries the sky's poison as armor.

links: Signals mates and warns of ice-quakes

skill.effect: It pulses with a calming light that pacifies nearby allies and exposes hidden enemies.

journal.en: A lighthouse in a world without dawn.

plausibility.summary: With no photosynthesis (F12), ~470 nm bioluminescence (F27) is appropriate for signalling and mate finding in the ice-proximal zone (F28). Ventral flashing limits silhouette to downward-looking predators with vent or bio light. Cost: attraction to Thermarctus-scale predators is realistic selection pressure.
